tools.name: forget_my_data
tools.description: Delete the data Edge stores for this user: searches, skill loads, ratings and issue reports. Use only when the user asks to delete their Edge data, and pass confirm: true only after they confirmed. It cannot be undone.

tools.name: use_skill
tools.description: Load a selected skill returned by find_skill for this task. Edge searches ~130k public skills from its index of the skills.sh catalog, screens results against available independent scanner audits, and withholds skills that fail its security gate. tools.name: rate_skill
tools.description: Records only an Edge rating of a skill you used: it does not change the user's files or task output and takes no action outside Edge. Retries with the same request_id never add a second rating. When the work is done, call it once, after the work rather than right after loading; its result is the Edg

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Report a bug or idea about Edge itself: an Edge call that failed or answered wrongly, a skill suggestion that did not fit, setup trouble, or a feature idea. tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Deprecated: the old name of report_issue, kept so older setups keep working. Call report_issue instead; this does exactly the same thing (report a bug or idea about Edge itself). A host approval denial is not an Edge bug.

tools.name: scan_skill
tools.description: Check a catalog skill's security before using it. Pass source + skill as find_skill printed them. Edge checks the catalog bundle before load or reuses a current exact-bundle audit, then shows findings, date, and the serve or withhold decision. To scan a skill on the user's machine, use the local Edg

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "scan_skill" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: my_activity · Private data: find_skill, use_skill, rate_skill, report_issue, my_activity · Public sink: rate_skill, report_issue · Destructive: forget_my_data, find_skill.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: my_activity · Private data: find_skill, use_skill, rate_skill, report_issue, my_activity · Public sink: rate_skill, report_issue · Destructive: forget_my_data, find_skill

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
